c1.note: CRN quotes a CDW spokesperson confirming organizational changes that included coworker reductions, with layoffs starting in July 2026.

c3.note: No passage was attached to this unit, but the CRN spokesperson statement confirms the reductions, and the Q3 call also cites a coworker component of the savings.

c4.note: CDW confirmed layoffs in July 2026, tied to the AI-first cost-savings program.

c5.note: This is the company's stated rationale, quoted verbatim in CRN.

c7.note: CRN states: 'The company did not disclose the number of impacted employees.'

c8.note: CRN opens with 'CDW in July initiated a round of layoffs, sources told CRN.'

c12.note: Analysts asked about layoffs on the Q1 2026 call in May, and CEO Leahy answered without denying them.

c14.note: The sources tie the layoffs to Geared For Growth, and the Q3 call cites a coworker component of the savings.

c17.note: CRN's wording is that CRN says the initiative will 'supercharge' the company; the quote is not attributed to Leahy, so the claim misattributes it.

c18.note: Crain's article dated July 22, 2025 has the headline 'CDW cuts more workers in fourth layoff round over 2 years'.

c19.note: CRN and itzbig both state CDW laid off between 450 and 750 employees in April 2023.

c23.note: Transcript: headcount reflects about 600 coworkers from Lovelytics.

c24.note: 10-Q for period ended 9/30/2026 is signed and dated November 4, 2026.

c25.note: 10-Q cites higher workplace optimization costs; CDW's definition includes workforce reduction costs, consistent with CRN's confirmed coworker reductions, though the definition text isn't in the passages.

c26.note: CDW's workplace optimization definition covers lease portfolio reduction charges; no passage shown, but consistent with CDW's known disclosures.

c27.note: Release's non-GAAP reconciliation defines workplace optimization this way; the passage shown doesn't quote it but it matches CDW's standard definition.

c29.note: CDW spokesperson confirmed coworker reductions to CRN and the 10-Q cites workplace optimization costs; CDW has had layoffs.

c10.note: The saved CRN page has no visible date. The itzbig rewrite is dated July 18, 2026, so a July publication is plausible, but July 16 is not confirmed.

c13.note: CRN says the initiative targets cost savings of up to $200 million. Search results from Seeking Alpha, Yahoo and Motley Fool give $100M–$200M run-rate savings into 2027–2028.

c15.note: The Q1 2026 earnings call was on May 6, 2026, and the program was discussed there. CRN also says the layoff question came up on the May call.

c20.note: The cited itzbig page has no 700 figure. A 600-700 figure from TheLayoff.com posts does exist, but it dates to the April 2023 layoffs, so it is unverified forum speculation and not a 2026 number.

c21.note: The claim is partly wrong on timing. CRN cites thelayoff.com only for layoffs 'last July', meaning 2025. TheLayoff posts about 2026 (for example thread 1kxqr8t49, July 17) concern the July 2026 round, and one search snippet mentioned an estimated 600-700 workers. I found nothing placing these posts

c28.note: The non-GAAP reconciliation shows workplace optimization of $75.2M for the nine months ended 9/30/2026 versus $15.5M a year earlier.

c31.note: The filing and the release give only dollar costs for workforce reductions and never a headcount. CRN and itzbig also report that CDW declined to say how many employees were affected.

c32.note: The footnote reads "Includes costs related to workforce reductions and charges related to the reduction of our real estate lease portfolio."

c33.note: The 10-Q only mentions workforce-reduction costs in footnotes and is not a layoff press release. The layoffs were confirmed by a spokesperson to CRN rather than announced by CDW. The claim that no separate announcement was found is consistent with the evidence.

c8.note: The CRN article says 'CDW in July initiated a round of layoffs, sources told CRN.' A CDW spokesperson confirmed there were 'coworker reductions' but did not say how many people were affected.

c12.note: CRN says analysts asked about layoffs on the Q1 FY2026 call in May. CEO Leahy answered that the savings would come from both productivity and cost cuts.

c14.note: CRN ties the cuts to the AI-first 'Geared For Growth' plan, which targets up to $200M in savings. On the Q3 call, the CFO said part of the Geared for Growth savings came from 'a coworker component.'

c30.note: CDW's Q3 2026 10-Q (period ended Sept 30, 2026), year-to-date comparison, says word for word: S&A rose $207M (8.6%), mainly from higher compensation including performance-based incentives, plus higher workplace optimization costs.
